ai.description: This 40–50 mm frog has a lime-green dorsum with scattered white spots. It features a distinct white subocular spot and a dark-edged, pale lateral stripe. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates occidentalis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged white spot on the tympanum, which is absent in other similar Indian tree frogs.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates occidentalis* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in moist vegetation at altitudes between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Charpa Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for insects among the foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates occidentalis* reproduces via foam nests deposited on vegetation overhanging water. They breed during the monsoon season, laying clutches of 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates occidentalis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Charpa Tree Frog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near forest streams or pools.
